title: AI agent cost estimator: what will an AI agent cost to run?
description: Price one AI agent for one workflow: set-up, monthly fees, your team's review time and a first-year total, low to high, every default sourced.
verdict: Most of the cost is people's time: set-up, training and checking the AI's work, not the model[^15][^17].
Ready-made support agents charge about $1 to $2 for each conversation they handle[^8][^10].
Turning on AI in software you already pay for costs $20 to $30 a person a month[^6][^5].
Model fees are rarely the biggest line: about $690 a month for 10,000 documents on a mid-tier model[^1][^3].
Messy data breaks budgets: Gartner expects firms to abandon 60% of AI projects without AI-ready data[^22][^21].

headings.what-it-is: What does an AI agent cost, and what drives it?
headings.faq: What do buyers ask about AI agent costs?

steps: Pick the one workflow you want an agent for, such as invoice entry, claims intake or customer emails.
Answer seven plain questions: volume, people, minutes per item, systems, data, risk and how you'd get it.
Read your first-year total first. Then check the line items, the two answers that widen the range and what you can skip.
Copy the link to share the estimate with whoever owns the budget.
method: Model fees = items × tokens per item × list price per million tokens × 1.15 for retries[^3][^1][^2]. Low, expected and high use small, mid and top-tier models.
Review time = items × share checked × minutes per check × $46.89 an hour, US pay plus benefits[^13][^16]. The share checked follows how bad a mistake is, a Zavient estimate.
Set-up uses published effort bands: 200 to 1,400 build hours and 3 to 5 days per connected system[^12][^11]. Outside work is priced at federal (GSA) schedule rates for AI work[^28].
Seat and per-conversation fees are list prices checked 26 Nov 2026 that still apply after 31 Dec 2026[^4][^5][^8][^10]. Promotions are left out.
Training is 10 hours per person, and upkeep on a custom build is 15% to 25% of the build a year[^14][^18][^19]. Lines marked Zavient estimate are our judgment around a published anchor.

summary: Running an AI agent costs cents to about $2 an item, or $20 to $30 a person a month in seats[^1][^8][^5]. Set-up, connecting systems and your team's time checking its work usually cost more[^11][^17].
humanRole: The ops lead who owns the workflow decides which items the agent may finish alone and which a person checks[^16].
The people who do the work today check the agent's output and handle the exceptions. Budget that time as its own line[^17].
The budget owner sets a monthly cap on usage fees, because they grow with volume and can sit on top of seat fees[^21][^27].

faq.q: How much does an AI agent cost?
faq.a: Usage runs $0.99 to $2 per conversation on ready-made support agents, or $20 to $30 a person a month for AI seats[^8][^10][^9][^5]. Set-up and people's time add more. Our worked example of 1,000 invoices a month comes to about $53,000 to $65,000 in year one on a ready-made path, a Zavient estimate[^14][^11].

faq.q: How much does it cost to build an AI agent?
faq.a: Published estimates put a custom agent at 200 to 1,400 hours of build work, plus 3 to 5 days per system it connects to[^12][^11]. Upkeep then runs 15% to 25% of the build each year[^18][^19]. Our worked example came to about $164,000 in year one, a Zavient estimate.

faq.q: Is the AI model the biggest cost?
faq.a: No, rarely: 10,000 documents a month cost about $35 on a small model, $690 on a mid model and $2,760 on a top model[^1][^3]. Training and checking the AI's work usually cost more[^15][^17].

faq.q: How much of the AI's work should people check?
faq.a: Check more where a mistake costs more: 27% of firms review all gen-AI output, and a similar share check 20% or less[^16]. Nearly 40% of AI time savings go to rework, so budget the checking[^17].

faq.q: Should we buy a tool, turn on AI we already pay for, or build?
faq.a: Most firms buy: 76% of AI use cases are bought, not built[^24]. Bought or partner-built tools succeed about 67% of the time, internal builds about a third as often[^25]. Build only when the work is core and no tool fits.

faq.q: How long does it take to get an AI agent working?
faq.a: Pilots on ready-made tools take 4 to 8 weeks[^20]. Half of firms take 3 to 6 months from idea to production, and Gartner's average is about 29 weeks[^20].

faq.q: Why do AI cost estimates go so wrong?
faq.a: Gartner warns that leaders who don't know how AI costs scale can be off by 500% to 1,000%[^21]. Usage grows with volume, and on some plans every token is billed on top of the seat fee[^27].

pickElse: Fewer than 10 people do this work: turn on AI seats you already pay for first[^5][^6][^7]. Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Business and Claude Team all qualify.
Your data is scattered or unknown: fix the data first. Gartner expects firms to abandon 60% of AI projects without AI-ready data[^22].
The agent would run a long chain of steps across systems: start with one step. Gartner expects over 40% of agentic AI projects to be canceled by 2027[^23].
Someone proposes training your own model: that costs $5 million to $20 million up front. Off-the-shelf models with your documents cover most first projects[^26].

offer.heading: Budgeting one AI agent? Check the number with us
offer.body: Want the detailed plan behind your result? Book the free 30-minute diagnostic.

reviews.notes: Wants one all-in number first. The result opens with the expected first-year total, then set-up, monthly fees and review hours, then the range. Fix: the total now states it includes your team's checking time, so it is not mistaken for the vendor bill alone.

Asked whether review time is new spend. It is time your current team already has, moved from doing the work to checking it. Fix: the review card now says so, and the hours today vs hours checking sit side by side.

Wanted to compare buy, turn on and build without rerunning. The three paths show side by side with set-up, monthly cost and time to first value; the cheapest is marked. Fix: added a Lowest cost label on that card.

Runs the tool. Items a month was unclear for document work; the help line now gives examples (emails, documents, tickets), and an exact number box sits under the ranges. Not sure answers stay allowed and widen the range instead of blocking.

Wanted to know if it pays back and what to skip. The result links to the AI ROI calculator and lists what can wait, such as a custom build under 10 people or training your own model. The range is wide on purpose; the two answers that widen it most are named.

answers.human-role: The ops lead decides which items the agent finishes alone, the people who do the work check its output, and the budget owner caps monthly usage fees[^16][^17][^21].
answers.faq: Buyers ask what an agent costs to run and build: $0.99 to $2 a conversation or $20 to $30 a seat a month, and 200 to 1,400 build hours[^8][^5][^12].
answers.something-else: Pick something else when fewer than 10 people do it, your data is scattered, the agent would chain many steps across systems, or someone proposes training your own model[^5][^22][^23][^26].
